QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_23

question.text: A covered call writer holds bonds at Rs. 100 and writes a call at strike Rs. 103 for Rs. 2.50. What is the breakeven point of this strategy?

explanation.text: The Logic: Covered call writing generates additional income from existing bond holdings and reduces the cost of acquisition; its breakeven is purchase price minus premium received (workbook pp. 180-181). Breakeven = 100 - 2.50 = Rs. 97.50. The Trap: Rs. 100.50 adds half the premium. Rs. 103 confuses breakeven with the strike. Rs. 100 ignores the premium. Note: The premium effectively cushions some price decline; below the breakeven the strategy turns into a net loss.
